I added `habit serve [port]`. It serves a page at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` listing each habit and its current streak, and it re-reads `habits.json` on every request so the page stays up to date. `npm test` passes (10 tests), including new ones for the page, habit names containing HTML, and the server's 200 and 404 responses. I haven't started the real CLI and opened the page in a browser.

The page is built by a new `page()` function in `src/commands.js`, and `src/server.js` serves it using Node's built-in HTTP module, so there are no new dependencies. The server only listens on your own machine (`127.0.0.1`), not the network. I also added one line to the README showing the new command.

Decision for you: port 3000 as the default, set with a positional argument, is my guess. The other options are a `PORT` environment variable or a `--port` flag. I'd keep the positional argument, since it matches how `[name]` already works.
